description:
We are a team of enthusiastic students participating in the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. We are interested in space science, technology, innovation, and problem-solving.

We welcome passionate and dedicated team members who are interested in learning, collaborating, and developing innovative solutions. Basic knowledge of Python, HTML, web development, design, research, or presentation skills would be an advantage.

We believe in teamwork, creativity, and learning together.
summary: Solar Explor is an interactive educational website designed to introduce students and beginners to the fascinating world of space. It provides simple explanations about stars, planets, moons, satellites, space exploration tools, and important space missions. The website includes five learning sections: Explore Space, Satellites, Space Tools, Space Missions, and an interactive Space Quiz. Our main goal is to make space science easy, interesting, and accessible to everyone, especially young learners. Through this project, users can explore basic space concepts, understand the importance of satellites and scientific instruments, and learn about important space missions in an engaging way.
details: Solar Explor is a web-based educational project designed to introduce students to space science and the history of space exploration. The website contains educational sections about planets, stars, satellites, space tools, and important space missions. It also includes an interactive quiz to help users test their knowledge. In connection with the challenge "Abandoned but not Forgotten," we aim to highlight NASA's equipment left on the Moon and Mars. Examples include Apollo lunar equipment, the Lunar Roving Vehicle, Spirit Rover, Opportunity Rover, and Viking Landers. The project explains what these machines were designed to do, the scientific information they helped collect, and why their missions eventually ended. We developed this project to make space history easier to understand for school students through a simple and engaging website. The website is hosted using GitHub Pages and is accessible through a public link.
